How long should a tattoo machine last? 👀

Asking for a friend… jk 😅 In all seriousness though, how long do you think a machine should last?

There are obviously a lot of variables — use, care, setup, quality, type of machine, etc… We’ve seen it all over the years. Artists still running coil machines we built in 2005 with little to no adjustment or repair, machines needing a refresh after 3–5 years of heavy daily use, and yes, the occasional rare issue much earlier than expected.

One thing we’ve always appreciated about coils and Kubins is the ability to rebuild, refresh, repair, and keep them going for years. Springs, contacts, bearings, motors, hardware, vises — these are machines that can actually be maintained and worked on, not just thrown away when something wears out.

At the end of the day, our goal has always been the same: build the best quality, longest lasting tools possible to help artists tattoo better.

Still at the core of everything we do is our old slogan — better tools for better tattooing. That idea is still in our hearts and hands every day we come to work.

What do you think? How long should a good quality machine last?

V46er Sidewinders — restocked. 💥
 
Fresh batch of @dankubin V46er Sidewinders just added to the site — a handful of different finishes available this round.

The V46er Sidewinder is a refined combination of the V4 through V6, redesigned and updated with years of building, tuning, and improving Sidewinders behind it.

A straightforward powerhouse.

Slightly more compact than most Sidewinders, with a little more stroke and a stronger hit. Still featuring the easy rear stroke adjustment wheel, allowing precise tuning from single needle work all the way up to large groupings and mag packing.

⸻

Performance-driven impact rotary with real snap off the tip for the crispiest bold lines.

Like snapping a wet towel — when the impact screw stops the armature on top of the frame, much like an armature stopping on top of a coil, that stored energy is delivered sharply to the tip of the needle.

That sudden stop creates a fast, clean hit with real snap off the tip — stronger penetration, cleaner saturation, and crisp, decisive lines.

This is what pens and other rotary machines try to emulate, but it’s hard to match when you’re just churning butter.

Yes, these machines can work well with cartridges, especially using Dan’s rubber band trick to help offset the upward force. But for the best performance and strongest linework, needle on bar tattooing — with the needle directly connected to the part generating all that force and impact — will always give you the best result.

Especially when paired with Dan’s Swift Tip setup 😎

More and more artists are moving off pens for the speed, power, and improved linework Sidewinders provide.

This month we’re under the starry skies of Kelowna, BC, to learn just how @Jillaine.tattoo gets her Northern Lights so bright… 

Jillaine Bergeson is doing for \"Great Outdoors\" tattoos, what Saga did for space tattoos... Her vibrant, full-colour Realism pairs incredibly well with landscapes, the night sky, and nature in general. FUCK…Makes you want to drop everything and just go camping.

Now 8 years into life as a tattooist, this Alberta-raised farm girl has made her way to Kelowna, BC and @district.ink.kelowna, where she uses her love for the outdoors to inspire her work (and it shows).

Almost as great as her passion for nature, is her passion for cover-ups.  Jillaine is always up for a challenge, and loves covering up those life mistakes we’ve all made at some point. This is why you’ll always find a box of Clear Cut Stencils on her station, because cover-ups are hard enough but placing your stencil shouldn't be. 

Outside the shop, Jilllaine can often be found snowshoeing across some of the landscapes she recreates, tossing discs into metal baskets (aka disc/frisbee golf), or kicking back to her favourite records while sipping on a warm cup of matcha.

Times have changed, today Colombia is now on the map, there are colombian tattooers winning prizes in conventions worldwide, and the young generations are doing amazing tattoos everyday. 
I really appreciate this recognition from @expotatuajemedellin, my hometown, and more than that, I feel really grateful with every person who has been part of this history, clients who give me the freedom to create something rare and special for them around the world, so many artists who share words about what they learned from my seminars and who I learned from, conventions who trust in my criteria to be their judge, and every person who has trusted in this process.

“It’s a good life if you don't weaken” - Gord Downie
